title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the open moduli spaces M_{0,I} of n = |I| ordered distinct points on P^1, with the symmetric group G_I acting. Ordinary Pic(M_{0,n}) is trivial: M_{0,n} is the complement of hyperplanes in A^{n-3}. So the interesting objects are equivariant line bundles, i.e. classes in H^1(M_{0,I}, G_I; G_m) = Pic of the quotient stack [M_{0,I}/G_I]. Such classes are torsion, and Grothendieck is computing their orders.

The line bundles: L_i is the cotangent line (psi-type bundle) at the i-th marked point. It is equivariant only for the stabiliser G_{I\{i}} of i. L = L_K = ⊗_{i∈K} L_i is fully S_n-equivariant. The second line records how L_i relates to L_K and to the pull-back, under the forgetful map p_{K\{i},K}, of the bundle L_{K\{i}} on the space with point i forgotten.

The table asks, for n = 4, 5, 6:
- the best (smallest) exponent making L equivariantly trivial: 3, 12?, 20?;
- the best exponent making L_i trivial (G_{I\{i}}-equivariantly): 6 (corrected from 5), 12?, 60?;
- these are compared with the guess (n-1)(n-2) = 6, 12, 20.
The bottom rows rephrase this as the exponent killing H^1(M_{0,I}, G_I·G_m), resp. H^1(M_{0,I}, G_{I\{i}}·G_m); these rows are left empty.

The computation on the right, for n = 5, is the upper bound 12:
- Take ⊗_{A∈P_4(K)} p_A^* L_A over all 4-element subsets A of K.
- On the open part, forgetting points does not change the curve, so p_A^* L_i^{(A)} = L_i.
- Each i lies in C(4,3) = 4 of the 4-subsets, so the product equals (∏_{i∈K} L_i)^{⊗4} = L^4.
- Since each L_A^3 is trivial (the n = 4 value), (L^4)^3 = L^{12} is trivial; this is S_5-equivariant because the family of all A is S_5-stable.

The problem served is to understand the torsion equivariant Picard group (characters and units) of the Teichmüller tower in genus 0, and its compatibility with the forgetful maps. This is the 'Lego' philosophy: building information up from the n = 4 and n = 5 levels.
errors: The n=5 argument only gives an upper bound: the order of L divides 12. Minimality is not proved, hence the '12?'.

The same induction for n=6 using 4-subsets gives L^{10}, whose cube is trivial, so the order divides 30; using 5-subsets gives L^{5·12}. Neither directly gives the guessed 20. The 20? and 60? entries are conjectural guesses patterned on (n-1)(n-2), not derived on the page.
The isomorphism L_i ≃ L_K ⊗ p^*L_{K\{i}} is stated without justification. Its exact meaning (e.g. whether L_K here has a different normalisation) is unclear from the page.

ideas.what: Torsion equivariant line bundles (psi bundles and their tensor product) on M_{0,n} under S_n, i.e. Pic of the stack [M_{0,n}/S_n] and of [M_{0,n}/S_{n-1}]
ideas.modern_name: Picard group of the stack of n unordered points on P^1 mod PGL_2; psi classes on M_{0,n}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Arsie–Vistoli (Pic of hyperelliptic stacks, 2004); Mumford (Pic M_{1,1} = Z/12, 1965); later work on Pic of unordered point stacks
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Teichmüller tower and M_{0,n} with S_n actions, but not these Picard torsion computations

ideas.what: Bounding the order of L_K by pulling back the n=4 bundles along all forgetful maps and counting incidences, (∏L_i)^{⊗4} = L^4
ideas.modern_name: forgetful-map compatibility of psi bundles on the open locus; inductive torsion bound

ideas.what: Conjectured order (n-1)(n-2) for the S_n-equivariant L
ideas.modern_name: order of the torsion Picard group of [M_{0,n}/S_n] (cf. the discriminant degree 2(n-1))

missed.claim: Grothendieck tabulates the orders of torsion equivariant line bundles on the genus-0 Teichmüller tower (S_n- and S_{n-1}-equivariant) for n=4,5,6. He conjectures a pattern related to (n-1)(n-2) and leaves the H^1(M_{0,I}, G_I; G_m) rows empty. This is an early (c. 1978-81) attempt at computing Pic of the stacks [M_{0,n}/S_n], later done by others (Arsie–Vistoli and successors) in the hyperelliptic / unordered-points setting.
missed.quote: meilleur exposant pour trivialiser L | 3 | 12? | 20? ... meilleur exp pour trivialiser L_i | 6 | 12? | 60?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a historical anticipation of the computation of Picard groups of moduli stacks of unordered points. It also links to Teichmüller-tower 'Lego', where n=4 relates to M_{1,1} and Z/12. Comparing his guesses with the known answers could be of interest, but no new theorem is present.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an unpublished but tentative table of equivariant Picard torsion orders on M_{0,n}/S_n, with conjectural entries. It foreshadows later stack-theoretic Picard computations, but contains no finished result beyond a routine upper bound.
transcription_corrections: In the row 'meilleur exp pour trivialiser L_i', the first entry 5 is overwritten by 6.
On the right, 'L_K and n=5' should read 'L_K and n=5' in the sense 'L_K for n=5'.
The right-hand computation reads ⊗_{A∈P_4} p_A^*(L_A), with 'p=3' noted under L_A (|A|=4, i.e. the n=4 exponent 3).
The struck-out row is 'exposant pour trivialiser H^1(M_{0,I}, G_I, G_m)'; the next row is 'trivialisant H^1(M_{0,I}, G_{I\{i}}, G_m)'.
The struck-out line above the table reads '12 ... 6' with p (exponent) marks.
